sanskrit: mi̱traṁ na yaṁ śimyā̱ goṣu̍ ga̱vyava̍ḥ svā̱dhyo̍ vi̱dathe̍ a̱psu jīja̍nan | are̍jetā̱ṁ roda̍sī̱ pāja̍sā gi̱rā prati̍ pri̱yaṁ ya̍ja̱taṁ ja̱nuṣā̱m ava̍ḥ ||
english: Him whom the diligent, who strive for cattle, have generated like Mitra among cows, of good understanding, in the assembly, in the waters — Heaven and Earth have trembled with his luster, with his song, in recognition of the dear, adorable one, the protection of creatures.

sanskrit: yad dha̱ tyad vā̍m purumī̱ḻhasya̍ so̱mina̱ḥ pra mi̱trāso̱ na da̍dhi̱re svā̱bhuva̍ḥ | adha̱ kratu̍ṁ vidataṁ gā̱tum arca̍ta u̱ta śru̍taṁ vṛṣaṇā pa̱styā̍vataḥ ||
english: When indeed the self-sustaining worshippers, like Mitras, have placed in honor that gift of yours, O Mitra-Varuṇa, for the Soma-pressing, much-besought one — then, O bull-like ones rich in dwellings, find the purpose, find the path; sing also what is famed.

sanskrit: ā vā̍m bhūṣan kṣi̱tayo̱ janma̱ roda̍syoḥ pra̱vācya̍ṁ vṛṣaṇā̱ dakṣa̍se ma̱he | yad ī̍m ṛ̱tāya̱ bhara̍tho̱ yad arva̍te̱ pra hotra̍yā̱ śimyā̍ vītho adhva̱ram ||
english: May the settlements adorn you, O bull-like ones — the birth of both Worlds is to be proclaimed for your great might. When you two carry it for Ṛta, when for the swift steed, when you lead the sacrifice forward with the priestly call, with the labor-song.

sanskrit: pra sā kṣi̱tir a̍sura̱ yā mahi̍ pri̱ya ṛtā̍vānāv ṛ̱tam ā gho̍ṣatho bṛ̱hat | yu̱vaṁ di̱vo bṛ̍ha̱to dakṣa̍m ā̱bhuva̱ṁ gāṁ na dhu̱ry upa̍ yuñjāthe a̱paḥ ||
english: That settlement, O Asura, which is the dear and great one — you two, the Ṛta-rich ones, proclaim Ṛta aloud and mightily. You two harness the encompassing power of high Heaven and the waters like a cow to the yoke.

sanskrit: ma̱hī atra̍ mahi̱nā vāra̍m ṛṇvatho 're̱ṇava̱s tuja̱ ā sadma̍n dhe̱nava̍ḥ | svara̍nti̱ tā u̍pa̱ratā̍ti̱ sūrya̱m ā ni̱mruca̍ u̱ṣasa̍s takva̱vīr i̍va ||
english: By your greatness you two open the great enclosure here; at the impelling place swiftly [come] dust-free milch-kine to the seat. They sound their note before the sun as it sets at dusk, like swift morning-birds at dawn.

sanskrit: ā vā̍m ṛ̱tāya̍ ke̱śinī̍r anūṣata̱ mitra̱ yatra̱ varu̍ṇa gā̱tum arca̍thaḥ | ava̱ tmanā̍ sṛ̱jata̱m pinva̍ta̱ṁ dhiyo̍ yu̱vaṁ vipra̍sya̱ manma̍nām irajyathaḥ ||
english: For Ṛta, O Mitra-Varuṇa, the long-haired ones have sung toward you, where you two set the path in motion with song. Release the streams of your own accord, swell the insights — you two rule over the thought-songs of the inspired poet.

sanskrit: yo vā̍ṁ ya̱jñaiḥ śa̍śamā̱no ha̱ dāśa̍ti ka̱vir hotā̱ yaja̍ti manma̱sādha̍naḥ | upāha̱ taṁ gaccha̍tho vī̱tho a̍dhva̱ram acchā̱ gira̍ḥ suma̱tiṁ ga̍ntam asma̱yū ||
english: The inspired poet-Hotṛ who worships you both, laboring with sacrifices, offering devotedly, accomplishing his song-thought — come to him nearby, traverse the sacrifice toward him; come with your songs, come with your benevolence, eager for us.

sanskrit: yu̱vāṁ ya̱jñaiḥ pra̍tha̱mā gobhi̍r añjata̱ ṛtā̍vānā̱ mana̍so̱ na prayu̍ktiṣu | bhara̍nti vā̱m manma̍nā sa̱ṁyatā̱ giro 'dṛ̍pyatā̱ mana̍sā re̱vad ā̍śāthe ||
english: You two, the Ṛta-rich ones, were first anointed by the sacrifices with cows, like the yoking of the mind's drives. The songs with their thought-weaving, restrained, carry to you — with unhaughty mind you two partake of abundance.

sanskrit: re̱vad vayo̍ dadhāthe re̱vad ā̍śāthe̱ narā̍ mā̱yābhi̍r i̱taū̍ti̱ māhi̍nam | na vā̱ṁ dyāvo 'ha̍bhi̱r nota sindha̍vo̱ na de̍va̱tvam pa̱ṇayo̱ nāna̍śur ma̱gham ||
english: You two bestow rich vigor, you two partake richly, O manly ones, guarding the great one with your powers through help. Neither the days, nor the rivers, nor the Paṇis have attained to your divine state, to your bounty.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ vastrā̍ṇi pīva̱sā va̍sāthe yu̱vor acchi̍drā̱ manta̍vo ha̱ sargā̍ḥ | avā̍tirata̱m anṛ̍tāni̱ viśva̍ ṛ̱tena̍ mitrāvaruṇā sacethe ||
english: You two clothe yourselves in rich garments; your counsels and your torrents are indeed without flaw. You have overcome all falsehoods — Mitra and Varuṇa, you follow Ṛta.

sanskrit: e̱tac ca̱na tvo̱ vi ci̍ketad eṣāṁ sa̱tyo mantra̍ḥ kaviśa̱sta ṛghā̍vān | tri̱raśri̍ṁ hanti̱ catu̍raśrir u̱gro de̍va̱nido̱ ha pra̍tha̱mā a̍jūryan ||
english: Even this their wise one does not discern — the true, poet-praised hymn strikes with rage. The fierce four-cornered one smites the triangular; the blasphemers of the gods have indeed perished from the very first.

sanskrit: a̱pād e̍ti pratha̱mā pa̱dvatī̍nā̱ṁ kas tad vā̍m mitrāvaru̱ṇā ci̍keta | garbho̍ bhā̱ram bha̍ra̱ty ā ci̍d asya ṛ̱tam pipa̱rty anṛ̍ta̱ṁ ni tā̍rīt ||
english: The footless one goes foremost of the footed — who among you, O Mitra-Varuṇa, perceives that? The embryo bears a burden even of this one; Ṛta rescues, untruth causes to fall.

sanskrit: pra̱yanta̱m it pari̍ jā̱raṁ ka̱nīnā̱m paśyā̍masi̱ nopa̍ni̱padya̍mānam | ana̍vapṛgṇā̱ vita̍tā̱ vasā̍nam pri̱yam mi̱trasya̱ varu̍ṇasya̱ dhāma̍ ||
english: We see the lover of virgins going forth, not coming near. Spread open, the beloved abode of Mitra and Varuṇa is clothed in never-shrinking garment.

sanskrit: a̱na̱śvo jā̱to a̍nabhī̱śur arvā̱ kani̍kradat patayad ū̱rdhvasā̍nuḥ | a̱citta̱m brahma̍ jujuṣu̱r yuvā̍na̱ḥ pra mi̱tre dhāma̱ varu̍ṇe gṛ̱ṇanta̍ḥ ||
english: Born without a horse, without a bridle, the strong one neighing flies upward on the summit. The young men have rejoiced in the unconscious sacred word, praising aloud in Mitra's domain, in Varuṇa's.

sanskrit: ā dhe̱navo̍ māmate̱yam ava̍ntīr brahma̱priya̍m pīpaya̱n sasmi̱nn ūdha̍n | pi̱tvo bhi̍kṣeta va̱yunā̍ni vi̱dvān ā̱sāvivā̍sa̱nn adi̍tim uruṣyet ||
english: The milch-kine coming forward, those of Māmateya helping, have swollen in this same udder, dear to the sacred word. Let the knowing one beg sustenance, having learned the laws; winning over Aditi as if pressing Soma, let him preserve her.

sanskrit: ā vā̍m mitrāvaruṇā ha̱vyaju̍ṣṭi̱ṁ nama̍sā devā̱v ava̍sā vavṛtyām | a̱smāka̱m brahma̱ pṛta̍nāsu sahyā a̱smāka̍ṁ vṛ̱ṣṭir di̱vyā su̍pā̱rā ||
english: I would turn toward you, O Mitra-Varuṇa, with homage and with protection, O gods, the acceptable oblation. May our sacred formula be victorious in battles; may our rain from heaven be easily fordable.

sanskrit: yajā̍mahe vām ma̱haḥ sa̱joṣā̍ ha̱vyebhi̍r mitrāvaruṇā̱ namo̍bhiḥ | ghṛ̱tair ghṛ̍tasnū̱ adha̱ yad vā̍m a̱sme a̍dhva̱ryavo̱ na dhī̱tibhi̱r bhara̍nti ||
english: We worship you two together in accord, with great oblations, O Mitra-Varuṇa, with reverences, with butter-offerings, O drippers of ghee — when the adhvaryus carry to us, to you, with their mental labors.

sanskrit: prastu̍tir vā̱ṁ dhāma̱ na prayu̍kti̱r ayā̍mi mitrāvaruṇā suvṛ̱ktiḥ | a̱nakti̱ yad vā̍ṁ vi̱dathe̍ṣu̱ hotā̍ su̱mnaṁ vā̍ṁ sū̱rir vṛ̍ṣaṇā̱v iya̍kṣan ||
english: The praise is your seat, not mere deployment — I have sent to you, O Mitra-Varuṇa, the fine hymn of praise. When the Hotṛ anoints you at the assemblies, the inspired patron wishes to sacrifice to your benevolence, O bull-like ones.

sanskrit: pī̱pāya̍ dhe̱nur adi̍tir ṛ̱tāya̱ janā̍ya mitrāvaruṇā havi̱rde | hi̱noti̱ yad vā̍ṁ vi̱dathe̍ sapa̱ryan sa rā̱taha̍vyo̱ mānu̍ṣo̱ na hotā̍ ||
english: Aditi the cow has given milk for Ṛta, for the people, O Mitra-Varuṇa, O givers of oblation. When the one who honors you impels you at the assembly — that man whose offering is given is like a human Hotṛ.

sanskrit: u̱ta vā̍ṁ vi̱kṣu madyā̱sv andho̱ gāva̱ āpa̍ś ca pīpayanta de̱vīḥ | u̱to no̍ a̱sya pū̱rvyaḥ pati̱r dan vī̱tam pā̱tam paya̍sa u̱sriyā̍yāḥ ||
english: And among the clans the inebriating Soma-plants, the cows, and the divine waters have swelled for you. And the ancient lord, granting this to us — drink deeply of the milk of the ruddy cow.

sanskrit: viṣṇo̱r nu ka̍ṁ vī̱ryā̍ṇi̱ pra vo̍ca̱ṁ yaḥ pārthi̍vāni vima̱me rajā̍ṁsi | yo aska̍bhāya̱d utta̍raṁ sa̱dhastha̍ṁ vicakramā̱ṇas tre̍dhoru̱gā̱yaḥ ||
english: Now I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu, who measured out the earthly realms, who propped up the higher station, striding in three steps — he of wide-going, praised on every side.

sanskrit: pra tad viṣṇu̍ḥ stavate vī̱rye̍ṇa mṛ̱go na bhī̱maḥ ku̍ca̱ro gi̍ri̱ṣṭhāḥ | yasyo̱ruṣu̍ tri̱ṣu vi̱krama̍ṇeṣv adhikṣi̱yanti̱ bhuva̍nāni̱ viśvā̍ ||
english: Viṣṇu proclaims this through his heroic might — a terrible wild beast who roams the mountains. In his three wide strides all beings dwell.

sanskrit: pra viṣṇa̍ve śū̱ṣam e̍tu̱ manma̍ giri̱kṣita̍ urugā̱yāya̱ vṛṣṇe̍ | ya i̱daṁ dī̱rgham praya̍taṁ sa̱dhastha̱m eko̍ vima̱me tri̱bhir it pa̱debhi̍ḥ ||
english: Let the praise-song go forth to Viṣṇu, the mountain-dweller, widely praised, the bull — who alone measured out this long, stretched-forth station with just three steps.

sanskrit: yasya̱ trī pū̱rṇā madhu̍nā pa̱dāny akṣī̍yamāṇā sva̱dhayā̱ mada̍nti | ya u̍ tri̱dhātu̍ pṛthi̱vīm u̱ta dyām eko̍ dā̱dhāra̱ bhuva̍nāni̱ viśvā̍ ||
english: His three steps are full of honey, inexhaustible, rejoicing through their own inherent power; who alone supports the triple-natured earth and heaven and all beings.

sanskrit: tad a̍sya pri̱yam a̱bhi pātho̍ aśyā̱ṁ naro̱ yatra̍ deva̱yavo̱ mada̍nti | u̱ru̱kra̱masya̱ sa hi bandhu̍r i̱tthā viṣṇo̍ḥ pa̱de pa̍ra̱me madhva̱ utsa̍ḥ ||
english: I would reach that dear station of his, where the god-devoted men exult — for that is truly the companion of the wide-strider: the fount of honey in Viṣṇu's highest step.

sanskrit: tā vā̱ṁ vāstū̍ny uśmasi̱ gama̍dhyai̱ yatra̱ gāvo̱ bhūri̍śṛṅgā a̱yāsa̍ḥ | atrāha̱ tad u̍rugā̱yasya̱ vṛṣṇa̍ḥ para̱mam pa̱dam ava̍ bhāti̱ bhūri̍ ||
english: We desire to go to those homesteads of yours where the many-horned, untiring cows are. Indeed there that highest step of the widely-praised bull shines down abundantly.

sanskrit: pra va̱ḥ pānta̱m andha̍so dhiyāya̱te ma̱he śūrā̍ya̱ viṣṇa̍ve cārcata | yā sānu̍ni̱ parva̍tānā̱m adā̍bhyā ma̱has ta̱sthatu̱r arva̍teva sā̱dhunā̍ ||
english: Your drink of the Soma-plant is set forth for him who thinks — sing also for the great heroic Viṣṇu, you two who stand undeceived on the mountain ridges in your greatness, like a swift horse on the right path.

sanskrit: tve̱ṣam i̱tthā sa̱mara̍ṇa̱ṁ śimī̍vato̱r indrā̍viṣṇū suta̱pā vā̍m uruṣyati | yā martyā̍ya pratidhī̱yamā̍na̱m it kṛ̱śāno̱r astu̍r asa̱nām u̍ru̱ṣyatha̍ḥ ||
english: Truly glorious is the encounter of the two vigorous ones — Indra and Viṣṇu; the Soma-drinker guards you both. You two who protect for the mortal what is being aimed at — you ward off the swift arrow of the archer.

sanskrit: tā ī̍ṁ vardhanti̱ mahy a̍sya̱ pauṁsya̱ṁ ni mā̱tarā̍ nayati̱ reta̍se bhu̱je | dadhā̍ti pu̱tro 'va̍ra̱m para̍m pi̱tur nāma̍ tṛ̱tīya̱m adhi̍ roca̱ne di̱vaḥ ||
english: They two increase greatly his manly power; the Mother leads him down to the enjoyment of the seed. The son places the lower and the higher, the father's third name upon the shining realm of heaven.

sanskrit: tat-ta̱d id a̍sya̱ pauṁsya̍ṁ gṛṇīmasī̱nasya̍ trā̱tur a̍vṛ̱kasya̍ mī̱ḻhuṣa̍ḥ | yaḥ pārthi̍vāni tri̱bhir id vigā̍mabhir u̱ru krami̍ṣṭorugā̱yāya̍ jī̱vase̍ ||
english: That and that manly deed of his we sing — of the sitting protector, wolf-free, the bountiful one, who strode widely on the earthly realms with just three strides, for the widely-praised one, for life.

sanskrit: dve id a̍sya̱ krama̍ṇe sva̱rdṛśo̍ 'bhi̱khyāya̱ martyo̍ bhuraṇyati | tṛ̱tīya̍m asya̱ naki̱r ā da̍dharṣa ti̱vaya̍ś ca̱na pa̱taya̍ntaḥ pata̱triṇa̍ḥ ||
english: His two steps visible to mortals — the mortal supports himself looking at them. Not even the flying birds can dare to reach his third step.

sanskrit: ca̱turbhi̍ḥ sā̱kaṁ na̍va̱tiṁ ca̱ nāma̍bhiś ca̱kraṁ na vṛ̱ttaṁ vyatī̍m̐r avīvipat | bṛ̱haccha̍rīro vi̱mimā̍na̱ ṛkva̍bhi̱r yuvāku̍māra̱ḥ praty e̍ty āha̱vam ||
english: Together with four and ninety names he shook out the interweavings like a wheel set in motion. Of great body, measuring with his praise-songs, the ever-youthful one comes forward to meet the call.

sanskrit: bhavā̍ mi̱tro na śevyo̍ ghṛ̱tāsu̍ti̱r vibhū̍tadyumna eva̱yā u̍ sa̱prathā̍ḥ | adhā̍ te viṣṇo vi̱duṣā̍ ci̱d ardhya̱ḥ stomo̍ ya̱jñaś ca̱ rādhyo̍ ha̱viṣma̍tā ||
english: Be you like Mitra, dear and blessed, with the pour of ghee, O abundantly-bright one, you who spread forward in the right course. Then, O Viṣṇu, even for the knower the praise-song is worthy, and the sacrifice is to be accomplished by the oblation-bearer.

sanskrit: yaḥ pū̱rvyāya̍ ve̱dhase̱ navī̍yase su̱majjā̍naye̱ viṣṇa̍ve̱ dadā̍śati | yo jā̱tam a̍sya maha̱to mahi̱ brava̱t sed u̱ śravo̍bhi̱r yujya̍ṁ cid a̱bhy a̍sat ||
english: He who offers to the ancient, ever-renewing, wise Viṣṇu with good knee-bending — he who proclaims the great birth of the great one, he shall indeed be united with glories, even with the noble.

sanskrit: tam u̍ stotāraḥ pū̱rvyaṁ yathā̍ vi̱da ṛ̱tasya̱ garbha̍ṁ ja̱nuṣā̍ pipartana | āsya̍ jā̱nanto̱ nāma̍ cid vivaktana ma̱has te̍ viṣṇo suma̱tim bha̍jāmahe ||
english: Let the praisers fill him up in accordance with ancient knowledge, the womb of Ṛta by birth. Knowing even his name, speak it out — of your greatness, O Viṣṇu, we partake of your benevolence.

sanskrit: tam a̍sya̱ rājā̱ varu̍ṇa̱s tam a̱śvinā̱ kratu̍ṁ sacanta̱ māru̍tasya ve̱dhasa̍ḥ ||
english: King Varuṇa follows that purpose of his, and the Aśvins follow the wisdom of the Marut-wise one. Dakṣa, the highest, knows the days; Viṣṇu, as companion, opens the cow-pen.

sanskrit: ā yo vi̱vāya̍ sa̱cathā̍ya̱ daivya̱ indrā̍ya̱ viṣṇu̍ḥ su̱kṛte̍ su̱kṛtta̍raḥ | ve̱dhā a̍jinvat triṣadha̱stha ārya̍m ṛ̱tasya̍ bhā̱ge yaja̍māna̱m ābha̍jat ||
english: He who, most well-doing among the well-doing, has yoked Viṣṇu for companionship with divine Indra — the wise one of three stations has sped the Ārya-man's noble work; in the share of Ṛta he has caused the sacrificer to partake.

sanskrit: abo̍dhy a̱gnir jma ud e̍ti̱ sūryo̱ vy u1̱̍ṣāś ca̱ndrā ma̱hy ā̍vo a̱rciṣā̍ | āyu̍kṣātām a̱śvinā̱ yāta̍ve̱ ratha̱m prāsā̍vīd de̱vaḥ sa̍vi̱tā jaga̱t pṛtha̍k ||
english: Agni has awoken; the sun rises from the earth; the bright dawn has greatly helped with her flame. The Aśvins have yoked their chariot to travel; the divine Savitṛ has impelled each living thing apart.

sanskrit: yad yu̱ñjāthe̱ vṛṣa̍ṇam aśvinā̱ ratha̍ṁ ghṛ̱tena̍ no̱ madhu̍nā kṣa̱tram u̍kṣatam | a̱smāka̱m brahma̱ pṛta̍nāsu jinvataṁ va̱yaṁ dhanā̱ śūra̍sātā bhajemahi ||
english: When you two, O Aśvins, yoke your bull-like chariot, sprinkle our sovereignty with ghee, with honey. Invigorate our sacred word in battles — may we partake of riches in the winning of the heroic.

sanskrit: a̱rvāṅ tri̍ca̱kro ma̍dhu̱vāha̍no̱ ratho̍ jī̱rāśvo̍ a̱śvino̍r yātu̱ suṣṭu̍taḥ | tri̱va̱ndhu̱ro ma̱ghavā̍ vi̱śvasau̍bhaga̱ḥ śaṁ na̱ ā va̍kṣad dvi̱pade̱ catu̍ṣpade ||
english: Let the three-wheeled, honey-carrying chariot of the Aśvins come hither well praised, with swift horses. The bountiful one with three seats, with all good fortune — may it bring blessing to us, to the biped and the quadruped.

sanskrit: ā na̱ ūrja̍ṁ vahatam aśvinā yu̱vam madhu̍matyā na̱ḥ kaśa̍yā mimikṣatam | prāyu̱s tāri̍ṣṭa̱ṁ nī rapā̍ṁsi mṛkṣata̱ṁ sedha̍ta̱ṁ dveṣo̱ bhava̍taṁ sacā̱bhuvā̍ ||
english: Bring us nourishment here, O Aśvins, you two; sprinkle us with your honeyed whip. Carry our lifespan safely across, wipe away harm, repel hatred — be you helpers who accompany us.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ ha̱ garbha̱ṁ jaga̍tīṣu dhattho yu̱vaṁ viśve̍ṣu̱ bhuva̍neṣv a̱ntaḥ | yu̱vam a̱gniṁ ca̍ vṛṣaṇāv a̱paś ca̱ vana̱spatī̍m̐r aśvinā̱v aira̍yethām ||
english: You two place the embryo in creatures, you two are within all the worlds. You two, O Aśvins, O bull-like ones, have set in motion Agni and the waters and the forest-lords.

sanskrit: yu̱vaṁ ha̍ stho bhi̱ṣajā̍ bheṣa̱jebhi̱r atho̍ ha stho ra̱thyā̱3̱̍ rāthye̍bhiḥ | atho̍ ha kṣa̱tram adhi̍ dhattha ugrā̱ yo vā̍ṁ ha̱viṣmā̱n mana̍sā da̱dāśa̍ ||
english: You two are indeed physicians with medicines; and moreover you are chariot-lords with charioteers. Moreover, O fierce ones, you bestow sovereignty upon him who offers you oblation devotedly in his mind.

sanskrit: vasū̍ ru̱drā pu̍ru̱mantū̍ vṛ̱dhantā̍ daśa̱syata̍ṁ no vṛṣaṇāv a̱bhiṣṭau̍ | dasrā̍ ha̱ yad rekṇa̍ auca̱thyo vā̱m pra yat sa̱srāthe̱ aka̍vābhir ū̱tī ||
english: O Vasus, O Rudras, of many counsels, growing mighty — O bull-like ones, O wondrous ones, honor us in the conquest. For the wealth of Aucathya is indeed yours when you two have flowed forth with your never-failing aids.

sanskrit: ko vā̍ṁ dāśat suma̱taye̍ cid a̱syai vasū̱ yad dhethe̱ nama̍sā pa̱de goḥ | ji̱gṛ̱tam a̱sme re̱vatī̱ḥ pura̍ṁdhīḥ kāma̱preṇe̍va̱ mana̍sā̱ cara̍ntā ||
english: Who shall offer to you for even this your benevolence, O Vasus, when you two sit with homage at the cow's footprint? Seize for us rich, understanding maidens — moving like one impelled by desire in his mind.

sanskrit: yu̱kto ha̱ yad vā̍ṁ tau̱gryāya̍ pe̱rur vi madhye̱ arṇa̍so̱ dhāyi̍ pa̱jraḥ ||
english: For indeed when Tugra's son Bhujyu was yoked to you, he was placed amid the ocean's midst — let me come to your shelter, O Aśvins; like a hero not through the currents in battle-courses.

sanskrit: upa̍stutir auca̱thyam u̍ruṣye̱n mā mām i̱me pa̍ta̱triṇī̱ vi du̍gdhām | mā mām edho̱ daśa̍tayaś ci̱to dhā̱k pra yad vā̍m ba̱ddhas tmani̱ khāda̍ti̱ kṣām ||
english: May Upastuta preserve the Aucathyan — may these two winged ones not milk me dry. May the tenfold-piled kindling not burn me, for I am bound in myself gnawing the earth when your bound one gnaws the ground.

sanskrit: na mā̍ garan na̱dyo̍ mā̱tṛta̍mā dā̱sā yad ī̍ṁ susa̱mubdham a̱vādhu̍ḥ | śiro̱ yad a̍sya traita̱no vi̱takṣa̍t sva̱yaṁ dā̱sa uro̱ aṁsā̱v api̍ gdha ||
english: The rivers most motherly have not swallowed me; the Dāsa slaves did not shake the tightly bound one loose. When Traitana cut off his head, the Dāsa himself gnawed into his own chest and shoulders.

sanskrit: dī̱rghata̍mā māmate̱yo ju̍ju̱rvān da̍śa̱me yu̱ge | a̱pām artha̍ṁ ya̱tīnā̍m bra̱hmā bha̍vati̱ sāra̍thiḥ ||
english: Dīrghatamas, son of Māmata, grown old in the tenth age — the Brahman becomes the charioteer of the purpose of waters, of those who strive.

sanskrit: pra dyāvā̍ ya̱jñaiḥ pṛ̍thi̱vī ṛ̍tā̱vṛdhā̍ ma̱hī stu̍ṣe vi̱dathe̍ṣu̱ prace̍tasā | de̱vebhi̱r ye de̱vapu̍tre su̱daṁsa̍se̱tthā dhi̱yā vāryā̍ṇi pra̱bhūṣa̍taḥ ||
english: With sacrifices I laud the great Dyāvāpṛthivī — Heaven and Earth, who augment Ṛta, O wise ones, at the assemblies. Those children of gods, those with divine offspring, with wondrous deeds — they adorn what is desirable with such intent.

sanskrit: u̱ta ma̍nye pi̱tur a̱druho̱ mano̍ mā̱tur mahi̱ svata̍va̱s tad dhavī̍mabhiḥ | su̱reta̍sā pi̱tarā̱ bhūma̍ cakratur u̱ru pra̱jāyā̍ a̱mṛta̱ṁ varī̍mabhiḥ ||
english: I regard the mind of the blameless Father as great, of the self-powerful Mother — with their libations; the two parents of good seed have established for progeny the broad immortal domain with their choosing gifts.

sanskrit: te sū̱nava̱ḥ svapa̍saḥ su̱daṁsa̍so ma̱hī ja̍jñur mā̱tarā̍ pū̱rvaci̍ttaye | sthā̱tuś ca̍ sa̱tyaṁ jaga̍taś ca̱ dharma̍ṇi pu̱trasya̍ pāthaḥ pa̱dam adva̍yāvinaḥ ||
english: Their sons, of good deeds, of wondrous power, have generated the two great Mothers for primordial perception. The path of the son, undivided in mind, is in the truth and ordinance of the standing and the moving.

sanskrit: te mā̱yino̍ mamire su̱prace̍taso jā̱mī sayo̍nī mithu̱nā samo̍kasā | navya̍ṁ-navya̱ṁ tantu̱m ā ta̍nvate di̱vi sa̍mu̱dre a̱ntaḥ ka̱vaya̍ḥ sudī̱taya̍ḥ ||
english: They, the wise ones of good insight, the skillful, have measured out the two kinswomen of one womb, the twins who share one dwelling. They weave ever anew the thread in heaven, within the ocean — the poets of bright flame.

sanskrit: tad rādho̍ a̱dya sa̍vi̱tur vare̍ṇyaṁ va̱yaṁ de̱vasya̍ prasa̱ve ma̍nāmahe | a̱smabhya̍ṁ dyāvāpṛthivī suce̱tunā̍ ra̱yiṁ dha̍tta̱ṁ vasu̍mantaṁ śata̱gvina̍m ||
english: That excellent bounty of Savitṛ divine we contemplate today at the god's impulsion. O Dyāvāpṛthivī, with clear insight bestow on us riches abounding in wealth, a hundredfold in cattle.

sanskrit: te hi dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī vi̱śvaśa̍mbhuva ṛ̱tāva̍rī̱ raja̍so dhāra̱yatka̍vī | su̱janma̍nī dhi̱ṣaṇe̍ a̱ntar ī̍yate de̱vo de̱vī dharma̍ṇā̱ sūrya̱ḥ śuci̍ḥ ||
english: For Dyāvāpṛthivī, they two — benevolent to all, Ṛta-rich, the two wise ones who hold the realm — between the two fair-born, auspicious ones the pure Sun god and goddess move in accordance with the ordinance.

sanskrit: u̱ru̱vyaca̍sā ma̱hinī̍ asa̱ścatā̍ pi̱tā mā̱tā ca̱ bhuva̍nāni rakṣataḥ | su̱dhṛṣṭa̍me vapu̱ṣye̱3̱̍ na roda̍sī pi̱tā yat sī̍m a̱bhi rū̱pair avā̍sayat ||
english: Of wide expanse, the two great inseparable ones — Father and Mother guard the worlds. The boldest among the bold, the two Worlds, as if for ornament — when the Father clothed her with his forms.

sanskrit: sa vahni̍ḥ pu̱traḥ pi̱troḥ pa̱vitra̍vān pu̱nāti̱ dhīro̱ bhuva̍nāni mā̱yayā̍ | dhe̱nuṁ ca̱ pṛśni̍ṁ vṛṣa̱bhaṁ su̱reta̍saṁ vi̱śvāhā̍ śu̱kram payo̍ asya dukṣata ||
english: He, the bearer, the son of the two parents, pure, purifies the worlds wisely with his power. The dappled cow and the bull of good seed have on all days milked his shining milk.

sanskrit: a̱yaṁ de̱vānā̍m a̱pasā̍m a̱pasta̍mo̱ yo ja̱jāna̱ roda̍sī vi̱śvaśa̍mbhuvā | vi yo ma̱me raja̍sī sukratū̱yayā̱jare̍bhi̱ḥ skambha̍nebhi̱ḥ sam ā̍nṛce ||
english: He is the most active of the active gods, who generated the two Worlds benevolent to all. He who measured out the two realms with his well-ordered wisdom has fitted them together with his never-aging props.

sanskrit: te no̍ gṛṇā̱ne ma̍hinī̱ mahi̱ śrava̍ḥ kṣa̱traṁ dyā̍vāpṛthivī dhāsatho bṛ̱hat | yenā̱bhi kṛ̱ṣṭīs ta̱tanā̍ma vi̱śvahā̍ pa̱nāyya̱m ojo̍ a̱sme sam i̍nvatam ||
english: O Dyāvāpṛthivī, you two great ones, when praised, shall bestow great fame, vast sovereignty. That wondrous strength with which we have spread ourselves over the peoples on all days — pour that power abundantly into us.
